source: test/e2e/shared-live.spec.mjs at the commit that adds this file's final hashes, Playwright 1.64.1 Chromium headless with SwiftShader, reduced motion; the run that produced them passed all four cases on desktop and phone
mode: family access on in-process servers bound to 127.0.0.1 with in-memory databases (and the real family runner for the restart case), live limits with a 1 s session re-check, empty provider keys, simulated payments and a FAKE Channel3 transport (invented products); each person a separate browser context with its own Chromium virtual authenticator; every request leaving the server origin refused and recorded (none were), with Channel3's image CDN answered by a drawn stand-in
limits: Test captures of synthetic people and households (Rowan, Ash, Wren, Fern), not real family use. The dropped connection is Chromium offline emulation plus the server closing its connections, not real network loss; the virtual authenticator is not a real device. No image shows an invitation link or token.
